name: Electrically Power-Assisted Cycle
description: New South Wales' e-bike since March 2026: a pedal cycle complying with the edition of EN 15194 that applied when it was made, so no more than 250 W, assisting only to 25 km/h and on a throttle only to 6 km/h. Until the end of February 2029 NSW also lets 200 W and 500 W e-bikes be ridden as bicycles; from 1 March 2029 this is the only one.

restrictions.rule: Two or more wheels, built to be propelled by human power through a belt, chain or gears, with an auxiliary motor; with that motor, a bicycle only if it complies with the requirements of EN 15194 (EN 15194:2017+A1:2023 as in force from time to time) that applied at its date of manufacture
No more than 250 W, no assistance above 25 km/h, and a throttle or walk assist that cuts out at 6 km/h
A vehicle with an internal combustion engine, or with any other auxiliary motor, isn't a bicycle
The only e-bike NSW treats as a bicycle, once the 200 W and 500 W alternatives lapse at the end of 28 February 2029
Riders follow the bicycle road rules, including an approved helmet; a rider 16 or older may ride on a footpath only while accompanying and supervising a child under 16 riding there
Since 21 August 2026 police and authorised officers may seize an illegal e-bike ridden on a road or road-related area and dispose of it
